seoTitle: Typeform Tutorial for Beginners: Getting Started Guide
metaDescription: A beginner's walkthrough of Typeform covering your first form, workflow branching, automations, and sharing to collect responses.
intro: Typeform's account is friendlier than most form builders on first login, but a blank workspace still leaves a beginner guessing where design ends and logic begins, and where the newer AI-assisted pieces actually fit in. This tutorial walks through starting from an empty workspace, building out a form's branching workflow, and connecting automations so responses go somewhere useful the moment they arrive — the parts of Typeform that matter more than which color theme you pick.

steps.heading: Start from My workspace
steps.body: Every new account lands on My workspace, which is also where every form you ever build will live. Typeform surfaces AI-suggested starting points right at the top — cards like "Monitor project milestones and team updates" or "Organize tasks and deadlines," each with a one-click Use this form button that clones a ready-made structure instead of making you start from a blank question list. A running counter on the left tracks your free-tier response limit, worth noting from day one since it caps how much real testing you can do before deciding on a paid plan.

image.caption: My workspace on a fresh account — AI-suggested form templates at the top, a free-tier response counter on the left, and Create form to start from scratch.

steps.heading: Build out the question flow
steps.body: Click Create form (or Use this form on a suggested template) to open the Content editor, where questions are added through the Add content panel and reordered by dragging them in the left-hand list. Every question type — Multiple Choice, Rating, Long Text, Payment, and dozens more — configures inline once added, so you can move from a blank form to a working question set without leaving the single editor screen. Beginners tend to over-ask; a form that answers one clear purpose with six well-chosen questions consistently completes better than one trying to capture everything at once.

steps.heading: Wire up branching in the Workflow tab
steps.body: The Workflow tab is where Typeform's real power shows — it renders the entire form as a visual chain of connected question nodes, with a Branching panel controlling which question a respondent sees next based on how they answered the last one. A sidebar on the right lists what you can attach to that flow: Connect actions that pull data into spreadsheets on submission, Automations that trigger based on the form's activity, and Contacts mapping that turns form fields into CRM-style records. This tab is what separates a static form from one that adapts — skip it and every respondent sees the exact same sequence regardless of what they've already told you.

image.caption: The Workflow tab's branching view — a connected chain of question nodes, with Connect, Automations, and Contacts panels on the right for wiring up what happens after submission.

steps.heading: Set up an automation for new submissions
steps.body: Under the Automations section, Create automation lets you define what happens the moment a response comes in — the panel tracks Form submissions and Contact activity/updates as trigger types, with more specific triggers marked Coming soon as Typeform continues building the feature out. Even a beginner-level setup, like emailing yourself or a teammate on every new submission, means you stop having to manually check the Results tab to know something came in. This is worth doing before the form goes live, not after — a form with no automation just becomes a dashboard nobody remembers to check.

image.caption: The Automations tab — Create automation alongside trigger types like Form submissions and Contact activity/updates for reacting to new responses automatically.

steps.heading: Use the built-in AI assistant where it actually saves time
steps.body: Typeform's AI tools sit inside the editor as a chat-style assistant — labeled "Chat to create" or "Ask Typeform AI" depending on where you are — that can draft a set of questions from a plain-language description of what you're trying to learn. It's genuinely useful for getting past a blank canvas or generating question phrasing you'd otherwise word clumsily yourself, but treat its output as a first draft: review every AI-generated question for tone and relevance before publishing, since it doesn't know your audience the way you do.

steps.heading: Preview, then publish and share
steps.body: Before publishing, click through the form in Preview mode exactly as a respondent would, testing any branching paths you set up in Workflow to confirm each answer routes correctly. Once it checks out, publish from the Share tab, where you'll find the direct link plus separate embed options for email and web pages. The form's link stays stable through future edits, so anywhere you share it now keeps working even as you refine questions later.

faq.question: Is Typeform free to start with?
faq.answer: Yes — the free plan lets you build and publish forms, but it caps monthly responses (visible as a running counter in your workspace), which is enough to test a form before deciding on a paid plan.

faq.question: Do I need design experience to make a good-looking form?
faq.answer: No. Typeform's built-in themes and AI-suggested templates handle most of the visual work, so you can adjust colors and branding without designing a layout from scratch.

faq.question: What is Typeform's Workflow tab used for?
faq.answer: It's where you set branching logic — which question a respondent sees next based on a previous answer — and where you connect Automations and Contacts so form activity triggers actions elsewhere.

faq.question: Can beginners use Typeform's AI features right away?
faq.answer: Yes — the AI assistant is built into the editor and can draft a set of questions from a plain description of your goal. Review its output before publishing, since it won't automatically match your audience's tone.

faq.question: What's the difference between Automations and Workflow branching?
faq.answer: Workflow branching controls what the respondent sees next inside the form itself. Automations run after a response is submitted — sending a notification, updating a contact record — and live in a separate Automations tab from the question flow.
